To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crystal structure of the Bacillus toxin Cry1Ac has now been solved, and that the structure of the complex of the toxin with its receptor ligand, N-acetyl-D- galactosamine, has now been determined to 2.95 Angstroms resolution.

the Cry1Ac toxin from Bacillus thurigiensis ssp. kurstkii HD-73 is crystallized as a monomer, that the receptor ligand GalNAc is bound in the crystal structure, that the toxin is a dimer in solution, and that the receptor-binding site is located at the dimer interface.
the crystal structures of Cry1Ac, the pore-forming toxin from B. thuringiensis, and of Cry1Ac complexed with the ligand GalNAc, have been solved at 2.36 A and 2.9 A resolution, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach to crystallization of Cry proteins and the use of this approach to solve the structure of the Cry1Ab toxin, which was the first insecticidal protein of this family to be crystallized.
the crystallization of the Cry1Ab toxin, which has been achieved by using 1,2-diaminopropan-2-ol (DAP) in place of 1,3-DAP as the buffer.
the crystallization of a protein toxin from B. thuringiensis and its complex with its receptor ligand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DAP is a very effective buffer in crystallization of proteins.
the use of 1,3-DAP is a very useful tool for the crystallization of Cry proteins.
the Cry1Ac protein is a pore-former, which is activated by proteolysis and then inserted into the membrane of the midgut epithelial cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cry1Ac crystallizes as a monomer and the GalNAc ligand is bound at a single receptor-binding site in the Cry1Ac monomer.

the crystallization of Cry1Ac has benefited from a combination of protein engineering, crystallographic screening and crystal optimization, and that the Cry1Ac crystal structure is a prerequisite for the determination of the structure of the Cry1A receptor binding domain and for the understanding of its mode of interaction with GalNAc.
Cry1Ac is a monomeric toxin in its active form and that the receptor ligand GalNAc binds at the trimer interface of the Cry1Ab toxin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cry1Ac trypsin-activation procedure is not a prerequisite to crystallization.
, in the absence of a suitable receptor, a Cry toxin can be crystallized in its monomeric form.
, in addition to the well-known effect of pH, the buffer used in the purification of proteins can also affect crystallization.
